node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/02-route-segment-config/instant.md 1 --- 2 title: instant 3 description: API reference for the instant route segment config. 4 related: 5 title: Next Steps 6 description: Learn how to use instant navigations in practice. 7 links: 8 - app/guides/instant-navigation 9 - app/getting-started/caching 10 - app/getting-started/revalidating 11 - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache 12 --- 13 14 The `instant` route segment config controls how Next.js validates whether a navigation into this segment would produce an instant UI. 15 16 Next.js uses prefetching to preload navigations for all in-app links on the current page. However, client-side data fetching or partially prerendered results from the server can lead to navigations that don't update the UI immediately. To help you build fast-feeling navigations, `instant` lets you tell Next.js what to expect from navigations through the configured segment. For instance, you can indicate that navigations into this segment should produce a UI that renders instantly without waiting on any externally loaded data. You can also indicate that navigations aren't expected to be instant. 17 18 When a segment is configured to expect an instant UI, Next.js surfaces any code in your application that would block the navigation from updating the UI immediately. See the [Instant Navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) for an end-to-end walkthrough. 19 20 > **Good to know**: 21 > 22 > - The `instant` export only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled. 23 > - `instant` cannot be used in Client Components. It will throw an error. 24 > - Next.js does not perform prefetches in development, so navigations may not feel as instant as they will in production. Validation reflects what will happen during `next start`, where prefetching is enabled. 25 26 ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx" switcher 27 export const instant = true 28 29 export default function Page() { 30 return
...
31 } 32 ``` 33 34 ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js" switcher 35 export const instant = true 36 37 export default function Page() { 38 return
...
39 } 40 ``` 41 42 ## Reference 43 44 The export accepts: 45 46 - **`true`**: Opts the segment into validation at whatever level is configured globally (see [Configuring validation defaults](#configuring-validation-defaults)). With the framework defaults, validation runs in development only and surfaces errors in the dev overlay. 47 - **`false`**: Opts the segment out (see [Disabling instant](#disabling-instant)). 48 - An **object**: Opts in with additional options. See [`level`](#level). 49 50 ### `level` 51 52 Sets the severity at which validation runs for this segment. 53 54 ```tsx filename="page.tsx" 55 export const instant = { 56 level: 'warning', 57 } 58 ``` 59 60 - **`'warning'`**: Validates in development only. Errors appear in the dev overlay; the build is unaffected. 61 62 In the future a validation level that supports validation during build will be supported. Unless you are enabling experimental validation modes there is no need to specify level since the only level available is `"warning"`. 63 64 When `level` is omitted (or `instant = true` is used), the segment is validated at whatever level is configured globally — see [Configuring validation defaults](#configuring-validation-defaults). 65 66 ### Disabling instant 67 68 Set `false` on a layout or page to indicate that this segment is allowed to block when navigating to it. 69 70 This is useful when a deeper page should be instant but an ancestor can't be. For instance, if a shared layout cannot load instantly but you still want to assert that pages beneath this layout can be navigated to instantly, you can ensure that the pages have `instant = true` while the shared layout has `instant = false`. 71

2  	title: Ensuring instant navigations
3  	description: Learn how to structure your app to prefetch and prerender more content, providing instant page loads and client navigations.
4  	nav_title: Instant navigation
5  	related:
6  	  title: Learn more
7  	  description: Explore the full instant API, caching, and revalidation.
8  	  links:
9  	    - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant
10 	    - app/guides/optimizing-prefetching
11 	    - app/getting-started/caching
12 	    - app/getting-started/revalidating
13 	    - app/guides/prefetching
14 	---
15 	
16 	This guide walks through understanding instant navigations, writing a route that navigates instantly, visualizing what's in the initial UI, and locking the behavior in with end-to-end tests.
17 	
18 	## What "instant" means
19 	
20 	A navigation is **instant** when the browser can start rendering the new page the moment the user clicks, with static, cached, and fallback content showing up right away, while the server streams the remaining content into its fallbacks.
21 	
22 	> **Good to know:** This definition assumes caches are warm. Cold caches still require the server to compute the cached result once, so the first navigation to a route may still wait.
23 	
24 	A direct visit and a client navigation to the same route can produce different initial UI. **Direct visits** get the [**static shell**](/docs/app/glossary#static-shell) as HTML, typically from a CDN. **Client navigations** only re-render below the layout the current and destination routes share, so the fallback UI defined by a `<Suspense>` boundary above that point can't be used during the transition.
25 	
26 	Whether the new page appears instantly depends on the `<Suspense>` boundaries and caching present below the shared layout.
27 	
28 	<details>
29 	<summary>Why page loads and client navigations produce different initial UI</summary>
30 	
31 	On a page load, the entire page renders from the document root. Every component runs on the server, and anything that suspends is caught by the nearest `<Suspense>` boundary in the full tree.
32 	
33 	On a client navigation between `/store/shoes` and `/store/hats`, only the components below the `/store` layout re-render. A `<Suspense>` boundary in the root layout covers everything on a page load, but on this navigation, it sits above the re-render scope and does not trigger.
34 	
35 	This is also why client-side hooks behave differently. `useSearchParams()` suspends during server rendering because search params are not available at build time. But on a client navigation, the router already has the params from the URL and the hook resolves synchronously. The same component can render immediately on a client navigation but sit behind a fallback on a page load.
36 	
37 	</details>
38 	
39 	With `prefetch={true}`, per-link prefetching resolves a link's URL data (`searchParams` and `params`) before navigation. First make the route instant with its App Shell. Per-link prefetching cannot fix a route that blocks without it. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) for the patterns.
40 	
41 	## Quick start
42 	
43 	Getting the most out of Instant Navigation requires enabling [Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components) and [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching), then following the [validation errors](#validate-instant-navigation) that appear:
44 	
45 	```ts filename="next.config.ts"
46 	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
47 	
48 	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
49 	  cacheComponents: true,
50 	  partialPrefetching: true,
51 	}
52 	
53 	export default nextConfig
54 	```
55 	
56 	To help you automate this process with an agent, there's a Skill for each part, [next-cache-components-adoption](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-cache-components-adoption) and [next-partial-prefetching-adoption](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-partial-prefetching-adoption).

1  	---
2  	title: Optimizing prefetching
3  	description: Resolve per-link URL data with the prefetch prop, include session data in the App Shell, or exclude expensive content from a prefetch.
4  	nav_title: Optimizing prefetching
5  	related:
6  	  title: Learn more
7  	  description: Validate your structure and review the caching primitives.
8  	  links:
9  	    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching
10 	    - app/api-reference/functions/prefetch
11 	    - app/api-reference/functions/navigation
12 	    - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch
13 	    - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant
14 	    - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private
15 	    - app/getting-started/caching
16 	    - app/guides/instant-navigation
17 	    - app/guides/prefetching
18 	---
19 	
20 	Prefetching downloads a route's JavaScript, CSS, and RSC payload before the user navigates to it, so the router can render the next route without waiting for a round trip. The [Prefetching guide](/docs/app/guides/prefetching) covers what the App Router prefetches by default.
21 	
22 	With [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) and [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching), a [`<Link>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link) prefetches one reusable [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route by default. The App Shell includes the route's static output. For routes that read [`cookies()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) or [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers), it also includes session-specific UI. Links to the same route reuse that App Shell.
23 	
24 	The shared App Shell does not include URL data that varies by destination, such as [`searchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#searchparams-optional) and [`params`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#params-optional). Set `prefetch={true}` on a link to resolve cached content that depends on its [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) before navigation instead of streaming that content after navigation.
25 	
26 	This guide assumes [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) with [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) enabled:
27 	
28 	```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={4,5}
29 	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
30 	
31 	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
32 	  cacheComponents: true,
33 	  partialPrefetching: true,
34 	}
35 	
36 	export default nextConfig
37 	```
38 	
39 	It also assumes your route is already structured for instant navigation. If it isn't, start with the [Instant navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) to validate its caching structure first.
40 	
41 	## Resolve URL data at prefetch time
42 	
43 	Set `<Link prefetch={true}>` to resolve URL data for that link before navigation. The destination must use [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching), enabled globally with `partialPrefetching` or per segment with [`prefetch = 'partial'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch#partial).
44 	
45 	A user on `/` sees links to `/search?q=react` and `/search?q=next`, each opting in with `prefetch={true}`:
46 	
47 	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx"
48 	import Link from 'next/link'
49 	
50 	export default function Home() {
51 	  return (
52 	    <nav>
53 	      <Link href="/search?q=react" prefetch={true}>
54 	        React
55 	      </Link>
56 	      <Link href="/search?q=next" prefetch={true}>
57 	        Next.js
58 	      </Link>
59 	    </nav>
60 	  )
61 	}
62 	```
63 	
64 	`'auto'` is equivalent to omitting `prefetch` or passing `undefined`. In a conditional expression, return `'auto'` for links that should keep the default App Shell prefetch:
65 	
66 	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx"
67 	<Link href={href} prefetch={isFeatured ? true : 'auto'} />
68

1  	---
2  	title: Optimizing prefetching
3  	description: Resolve per-link URL data with the prefetch prop, include session data in the App Shell, or exclude expensive content from a prefetch.
4  	nav_title: Optimizing prefetching
5  	related:
6  	  title: Learn more
7  	  description: Validate your structure and review the caching primitives.
8  	  links:
9  	    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching
10 	    - app/api-reference/functions/prefetch
11 	    - app/api-reference/functions/navigation
12 	    - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch
13 	    - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant
14 	    - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private
15 	    - app/getting-started/caching
16 	    - app/guides/instant-navigation
17 	    - app/guides/prefetching
18 	---
19 	
20 	Prefetching downloads a route's JavaScript, CSS, and RSC payload before the user navigates to it, so the router can render the next route without waiting for a round trip. The [Prefetching guide](/docs/app/guides/prefetching) covers what the App Router prefetches by default.
21 	
22 	With [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) and [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching), a [`<Link>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link) prefetches one reusable [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route by default. The App Shell includes the route's static output. For routes that read [`cookies()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) or [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers), it also includes session-specific UI. Links to the same route reuse that App Shell.
23 	
24 	The shared App Shell does not include URL data that varies by destination, such as [`searchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#searchparams-optional) and [`params`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#params-optional). Set `prefetch={true}` on a link to resolve cached content that depends on its [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) before navigation instead of streaming that content after navigation.
25 	
26 	This guide assumes [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) with [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) enabled:
27 	
28 	```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={4,5}
29 	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
30 	
31 	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
32 	  cacheComponents: true,
33 	  partialPrefetching: true,
34 	}
35 	
36 	export default nextConfig
37 	```
38 	
39 	It also assumes your route is already structured for instant navigation. If it isn't, start with the [Instant navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) to validate its caching structure first.
40 	
41 	## Resolve URL data at prefetch time
42 	
43 	Set `<Link prefetch={true}>` to resolve URL data for that link before navigation. The destination must use [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching), enabled globally with `partialPrefetching` or per segment with [`prefetch = 'partial'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch#partial).
44 	
45 	A user on `/` sees links to `/search?q=react` and `/search?q=next`, each opting in with `prefetch={true}`:
46 	
47 	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx"
48 	import Link from 'next/link'
49 	
50 	export default function Home() {
51 	  return (
52 	    <nav>
53 	      <Link href="/search?q=react" prefetch={true}>
54 	        React
55 	      </Link>
56 	      <Link href="/search?q=next" prefetch={true}>
57 	        Next.js
58 	      </Link>
59 	    </nav>
60 	  )
61 	}
62 	```
63 	
64 	`'auto'` is equivalent to omitting `prefetch` or passing `undefined`. In a conditional expression, return `'auto'` for links that should keep the default App Shell prefetch:
65 	
66 	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx"
67 	<Link href={href} prefetch={isFeatured ? true : 'auto'} />

197	## Exclude content from a prefetch
198	
199	Optimizing a prefetch also means excluding content from it. Some subtrees are expensive enough to produce that you would rather not pay for them on every prefetch of the route.
200	
201	Awaiting [`navigation()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/navigation) above the work leaves it out of every prefetch, so it is produced on the navigation. The nearest [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) fallback is what the user sees while it streams in. Take the dashboard again, where a ranking keyed on the session is too expensive to produce for every link into the route:
202	
203	```tsx filename="app/dashboard/recommendations.tsx" highlight={6}
204	import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
205	import { navigation } from 'next/cache'
206	
207	async function Recommendations() {
208	  const session = (await cookies()).get('session')?.value
209	  await navigation()
210	  const items = await rank(session)
211	  return <List items={items} />
212	}
213	
214	async function rank(session?: string) {
215	  'use cache: private'
216	  return db.recommendations.rank({ session })
217	}
218	```
219	
220	The session is read above `navigation()`, so it resolves in the shell like any other session data. Only the ranking is left out, and it keeps its cache lifetime.
221	
222	Without it, keeping a subtree out of a prefetch means leaving it uncached, which gives up that lifetime on the navigation too. Awaiting `navigation()` inside a cached scope is not allowed, so put the caching directive on a function called below it, as `rank` does here.
223	
224	For a subtree that would otherwise sit in the App Shell, but that a `<Link prefetch={true}>` should still resolve before the click, use [`prefetch()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch) instead.
225	
226	Unlike [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection), `navigation()` does not make the subtree request-dependent. This lets reusable content keep its cache lifetime while waiting for navigation. See [How `navigation()` differs from `connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/navigation#how-navigation-differs-from-connection) for the full comparison.
227	
228	## Test prefetched and deferred content
229	
230	The [Instant navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) explains how to install and configure `@next/playwright`. For a client navigation, use `instant()` to inspect the destination's prefetched UI.
231	
232	When [adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests), run this test before enabling the feature and rerun the same assertions afterward. This preserves the UI selected from the legacy full prefetch while its implementation moves to the App Shell or a per-link prefetch.
233	
234	Inside the callback, click the link, wait for the destination URL, and assert which content is available. After the callback releases the navigation, assert that deferred content eventually renders:
235	
236	```ts filename="e2e/product-navigation.test.ts" highlight={8-15,17}
237	import { expect, test } from '@playwright/test'
238	import { instant } from '@next/playwright'
239	
240	test('prefetches the product summary but not reviews', async ({ page }) => {
241	  await page.goto('/products')
242	
243	  await instant(page, async () => {
244	    await page.click('a[href="/products/baseball-cap"]')
245	    await page.waitForURL((url) => url.pathname === '/products/baseball-cap')
246	
247	    await expect(
248	      page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Baseball Cap' })
249	    ).toBeVisible()
250	    await expect(page.getByTestId('product-summary')).toBeVisible()
251	    await expect(page.getByTestId('reviews')).toHaveCount(0)
252	  })
253	
254	  await expect(page.getByTestId('reviews')).toBeVisible()
255	})
256	```
257

1  	---
2  	title: Adopting Partial Prefetching
3  	nav_title: Adopting Partial Prefetching
4  	description: Learn how to enable Partial Prefetching and what changes for `<Link>`.
5  	related:
6  	  title: Next Steps
7  	  description: Learn more about prefetching and instant navigations.
8  	  links:
9  	    - app/guides/instant-navigation
10 	    - app/guides/optimizing-prefetching
11 	    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching
12 	    - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch
13 	    - app/api-reference/functions/prefetch
14 	    - app/api-reference/functions/navigation
15 	---
16 	
17 	[Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.
18 	
19 	To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.
20 	
21 	Along the way, Next.js surfaces [instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) insights in development, naming the link or route to change.
22 	
23 	> **Good to know**: Partial Prefetching only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.
24 	
25 	## Use the adoption skill (recommended)
26 	
27 	The [`next-partial-prefetching-adoption`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/skills/next-partial-prefetching-adoption) skill drives this adoption with a coding agent. It reviews your `<Link prefetch={true}>` calls, captures the prefetched UI to preserve with [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) when a production test rig is available, then enables the flag and checks each route for the insights this guide covers.
28 	
29 	Install the skill:
30 	
31 	```bash filename="Terminal"
32 	npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-adoption
33 	```
34 	
35 	Then give the agent this prompt:
36 	
37 	```prompt
38 	Adopt Partial Prefetching in this project using the next-partial-prefetching-adoption skill.
39 	```
40 	
41 	## Or adopt by hand
42 	
43 	To adopt an existing app by hand:
44 	
45 	1. [Review existing full prefetches](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) and choose which part of each destination should continue to be prefetched. You can use [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) to add regression coverage.
46 	2. [Enable `partialPrefetching`](#enable-partial-prefetching). For larger migrations, you can [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) with the global flag off. The [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight identifies each destination that still uses the legacy full prefetch.
47 	3. [Move URL data behind Suspense](#move-url-data-behind-suspense), resolving the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight.
48 	4. Optionally, [prefetch URL data](#prefetching-url-data) on the routes where streaming in after navigation isn't enough.
49 	5. Optionally, [exclude cached content from a prefetch](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#exclude-content-from-a-prefetch) on the routes where caching content into the App Shell made it heavier than you want.
50 	
51 	Both insights are development-only and never block the build. They appear in the dev overlay with fix cards that link the docs page for each fix. If a route isn't ready to adopt, export [`instant = false`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route

267	
268	### URL data
269	
270	[URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) varies per link, so content that depends on it can't be included in the shared App Shell and streams in after navigation from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary. The links keep `prefetch={true}`, and [Prefetching URL data](#prefetching-url-data) covers prefetching the content ahead of the click.
271	
272	### Real-time content
273	
274	A prefetch of real-time content would be stale by the click, so there is nothing to preserve. Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary.
275	
276	| Destination                                                                       | Recommendation                                                            |
277	| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
278	| [Fully static, or content already cached](#static-or-cached-content)              | Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`.                               |
279	| [Delivered uncached content you want kept ahead of the click](#uncached-content)  | Cache it with `use cache`, then remove `prefetch={true}`.                 |
280	| [Delivered content that depends on `cookies()` or `headers()`](#session-content)  | Cache the lookup behind the session value, then remove `prefetch={true}`. |
281	| [Reads URL data, or has cached content that depends on it](#url-data)             | Keep `prefetch={true}` to resolve the content ahead of the click.         |
282	| [Delivers real-time content that must stay fresh per request](#real-time-content) | Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in.                   |
283	
284	## Adopting incrementally
285	
286	Adoption doesn't have to happen in one change. [`prefetch = 'partial'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) is the global flag scoped to one route, so with the global flag still off, you can adopt and deploy each destination on its own.
287

1 	---
2 	title: partialPrefetching
3 	description: Configure the default link prefetch behavior to fetch only the static parts of each route.
4 	related:
5 	  title: Related
6 	  description: View related API references and guides.
7 	  links:
8 	    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents
9 	    - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch
10	    - app/api-reference/components/link
11	    - app/guides/optimizing-prefetching
12	---
13	
14	`partialPrefetching` enables Partial Prefetching at the app level. The framework prefetches the static parts of each route by default; set `prefetch={true}` on individual links to use [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) and fetch more.
15	
16	## Usage
17	
18	```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5} switcher
19	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
20	
21	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
22	  cacheComponents: true,
23	  partialPrefetching: true,
24	}
25	
26	export default nextConfig
27	```
28	
29	```js filename="next.config.js" highlight={3} switcher
30	module.exports = {
31	  cacheComponents: true,
32	  partialPrefetching: true,
33	}
34	```
35	
36	`partialPrefetching` requires [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents). Without it, `next dev` and `next build` throw at config validation.
37	
38	## Reference
39	
40	| Value   | Description                                 |
41	| ------- | ------------------------------------------- |
42	| `true`  | Enables Partial Prefetching across the app. |
43	| `false` | Default. No change to prefetch behavior.    |
44	
45	## How prefetches resolve
46	
47	Before Partial Prefetching, Next.js prefetched per visible link: a page with N links to N routes produced ~N route prefetches as those links entered the viewport.
48	
49	With `partialPrefetching: true`, Next.js prefetches one reusable [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route instead. The App Shell contains rendered output that does not depend on a link's URL. URL-specific content, including content that depends on `params` or `searchParams`, resolves after navigation by default. App Shells are cached on the client, so links to the same route reuse one prefetch.
50	
51	The pattern is similar to per-route code splitting in single-page apps: one artifact per route, shared by every link that points to it.
52	
53	> **Good to know**: Routes that read `cookies()` or `headers()` produce an App Shell that includes session data. The framework auto-detects this and caches the shell per session on the client.
54	
55	A link can ask for more than the App Shell with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch also resolves URL data like `params`, `searchParams`, and the full URL, and the cached content behind it. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching).
56	
57	> **Good to know**: If you use `<Link prefetch={true}>` to a route that hasn't opted into Partial Prefetching, a dev console error suggests enabling `partialPrefetching` app-wide or `prefetch = 'partial'` on the segment. The [dev warning Insight](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) covers each fix in detail.
58	
59	## Per-segment overrides
60	
61	A segment that exports an explicit [`prefetch`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) value overrides the app-level default for that route.
62	
63	## Version History
64	
65	| Version | Change                                                                     |
66	| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
67	| 16.3.0  | `partialPrefetching` introduced. Requires `cacheComponents` to be enabled. |
</content>

python3 - << 'PY'
import urllib.request, time

def fetch(label, headers):
    req = urllib.request.Request('http://127.0.0.1:3456/projects/acme', headers=headers)
    start = time.perf_counter()
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=15) as res:
            body = res.read()
            elapsed = (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000
            text = body.decode('utf-8', 'replace')
            print('===', label, '===')
            print('status', res.status, 'ms', round(elapsed), 'len', len(body))
            print('final url', res.geturl())
            interesting = ['Acme Storefront', 'Commerce storefront', 'Production deployment', 'Loading project', 'Recent activity']
            for s in interesting:
                print(f'  contains {s!r}:', s in text)
            print('--- body snippet ---')
            print(text[:1500])
            print()
    except Exception as e:
        elapsed = (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000
        print('===', label, 'ERROR', type(e).__name__, e, 'ms', round(elapsed))
        if hasattr(e, 'headers'):
            print('location', e.headers.get('location'))
            print('code', getattr(e, 'code', None))

common = {
    'rsc': '1',
    'accept': 'text/x-component',
}
fetch('full rsc', common)
fetch('prefetch 1', {**common, 'next-router-prefetch': '1'})
fetch('prefetch 2', {**common, 'next-router-prefetch': '2'})
fetch('prefetch 3', {**common, 'next-router-prefetch': '3'})
fetch('segment tree', {**common, 'next-router-prefetch': '1', 'next-router-segment-prefetch': '/_tree'})
PY

events.content:
Navigating from the dashboard now shows the project title immediately, without prefetching the rest of the page.

Dashboard links use `prefetch={true}`, so the cached title is ready before the click. The description and activity sit behind `navigation()`, so they render only after navigation. Partial prefetching is on, which keeps that per-link prefetch from pulling the whole route.

`npx next build` passed with exit code 0. A production prefetch of `/projects/acme` included "Acme Storefront" and omitted the description and activity. A full navigation still returned both.
